newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN FORD HAS 1996 LOSS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN FORD HAS 1996 LOSS - PAPER.

text.p: The Belgian car assembly plant of Ford of the U.S. lost 2.87 billion Belgian francs in 1996, while turnover dropped by 23 bilion francs to 155 billion, Belgian paper Het Belang van Limburg said on Friday.

Quoting what it called confidential company documents, the paper said the Ford plant in the town of Genk, which resorts under Cologne, Germany, based Ford Werke AG, assembled a total 437,000 Mondeo cars and Transit vans in 1996.
Last year's sales were the lowest since 1992 when a figure of 120 billion francs was booked. Sales peaked in 1994 at 183 billion francs, easing to 178 billion francs in 1995.
The bulk of Ford Genk's production goes to the U.K. with Germany a close second. Only 3.4 percent stays in Belgium.

The paper said Ford Werke AG, which also includes a plant in Saarlouis, Germany, lost 551 million marks in 1996 on sales of 26.4 billion marks as a result of a shift in demand to smaller, low-profit cars and pressure on margins from rising competition.
The paper quoted the documents as saying global overcapacity in the car industry stood at over 30 percent, or a surplus of more than 60 car plants.
